correctness.rationale: An exact independent-failure formula leads to strict fixed-size sex balancing; a geometric-mean failure inequality rules out odd allocations; strict concavity in S=t^j+t^(n-j) restricts paired optima to concentration or near-half division; direct comparison determines every tie and the even-budget strictly monotone bracket gives the unique closed threshold. The source checker verifies 13,088 exact-fraction allocations for n=1..12 and sixteen parameter settings. Boundary exclusions and one-step feasibility scope are explicit; finite checks do not replace the general algebra.

originality.rationale: published-record queries of same-sex founder allocation, mate-limited establishment, habitat-insurance, and single-large-versus-divided introductions produced no matching two-site all-allocation theorem. The closest primary literature addresses stochastic establishment or release numbers/sizes with different model features, and does not demonstrably imply the exact two-site sex-balanced classification or sharp threshold. This is a literature-based self-review, not proof of global absence; unresolved access risks are named.

value.rationale: This model isolates a meaningful conservation allocation conflict: mates require co-location, while independent habitat suitability favors diversification. It gives a complete nontrivial global classification for every integer two-sex founder budget, rules out all intermediate unequal releases, identifies exact tie surfaces and provides a closed sharp even-budget environmental-insurance threshold with founder-number asymptotics. It does not claim realistic long-term persistence; its value is an exact benchmark for richer models.
